fullPassage: At least one billion people, or 15% of the world’s population, experience some form of disability. In order to fully function in everyday life, they need to have the same physical and social access to the places, goods, and services in their communities as everyone else. For many of them, however, access still remains an issue. Here are two teenagers who presented new inventions to tackle the issue at an international science competition. 3D Braille Map While thinking about her homework, Seoyoung Jun closed one eye and successfully picked up her pencil holder. At that moment, she realized that orienting herself in a 3D space didn’t require both eyes. This surprised her. With research, she learned that the brain can process 3D information without any vision at all. And with that, the idea for a new device for people with visual disabilities was born. Those who have lost sight get their spatial information mainly from touch, not vision. She based her new navigation device on this fact. This little device sends a beam of infrared light to gather 3D information about what may lie around the user, including walls and furniture. The bounced beam conveys that information to the device, which then raises little pins to indicate where those obstacles are. By “reading” the positions and heights of those pins, the user can understand the arrangement of structures and objects lying ahead and navigate around them. The heart of this device is a 3D depth sensor connected to a small computer. Seoyoung coded the computer to control the nine motors lined up in three rows of three so that each motor could move a pin up and down. The sensor can scan eighteen blocks of space before it, each 0.06㎥ in size. When it detects an obstacle in any of these blocks, the corresponding pin rises to either the middle or high position, depending on the height of the obstacle. By running your hand over the nine pins, you can tell where the obstacles are and how high they are. When Seoyoung’s device worked for the first time, she didn’t believe it. To be sure it wasn’t a mistake, she shut it off and rebooted it. When it worked again, she started screaming with joy. It had been seven long months of research, building, and testing. She imagines a future version that could be connected to a smartphone, with more pins and more height positions. Sign Language-to-Speech App As a coder, Nand Vinchhi wanted to invent something that didn’t require a mechanical device. One day, he was brainstorming with friends, and the group came up with an idea for an app that could translate sign language. In the end, they decided not to develop it, but Nand couldn’t stop thinking about the translator. In just a few months, he developed an app based on artificial intelligence for translating American Sign Language (ASL) in real time. Nand’s app was basically a speech-to-text app for sign language, where hand movements corresponded to speech. The hardest part was figuring out how to make the app recognize hand gestures. At times, he felt he was stuck. When that happened, he would go to sleep. For Nand, sleeping on it paid off. He decided to focus on the body parts which are important in signing, such as individual fingertips. Using a machine-learning program, he then taught the app to identify those key points in the videos he took. When the user runs the app, gestures are captured by the camera. Then, the app uses an algorithm to match the movements with words in ASL, which are turned into text and then spoken aloud. According to Nand, his system now translates signs with 90.4% accuracy, and the delay from signing to translation is only about three-tenths of a second. He imagines the technology could someday become part of existing communication platforms. That could help ASL speakers communicate with those who don’t know the language. What these inventions have in common is a creative use of technology to enhance the daily lives of people with disabilities. Their efforts will go a long way toward a more accessible world for all. Read More Self-Driving Cars Cars are now making steps toward their own kind of freedom; that is, freedom from people. The goal is to build a car that uses artificial intelligence so that it thinks and drives like a human. The technology for a self-driving car has reached the point where it is becoming increasingly accessible. Self-driving cars have clear advantages. Most of all, sitting behind the wheel would no longer be limited by age or ability. For example, a person who has lost sight could rely on a self-driving car to go from one place to another. Furthermore, most accidents are caused by careless people on the road. For example, many crashes are caused by people using their phones while driving, falling asleep at the wheel, or driving while drunk. With a self-driving car, people would not need to worry about such situations on the road. However, there are also some serious concerns when it comes to the safety of self-driving cars, since the technology is still far from perfect. In fact, a self-driving car depends only on its sensors, GPS, and computer programs to work properly. If any of these broke down or were used for unintended purposes, then the safety and security of the rider as well as other people on the road could be put at risk.

Nand는 수화에서 중요한 신체 부위, 특히 개별 손가락 끝에 집중하기로 했다.

questions.passage: Nand’s app was basically a speech-to-text app for sign language, where hand movements ①<u>corresponded</u> to speech.  The hardest part was figuring out how to make the app ②<u>to recognize</u> hand gestures.  At times, he felt he was ③<u>stuck</u>.  When that happened, he would ④<u>go</u> to sleep.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① corresponded: 관계사절의 주어 hand movements에 맞춘 과거시제 동사 corresponded로 적절
❌ ② to recognize → recognize: 사역동사 make의 목적격 보어 자리이므로 원형부정사 recognize가 옳다. to부정사 to recognize는 부적절 ←정답
✅ ③ stuck: felt의 보어로 '막힌 상태인'을 나타내는 형용사 stuck으로 적절
✅ ④ go: 조동사 would 뒤에 오는 동사원형 go로 적절
det.tip: 사역동사 make의 목적격 보어에는 to를 붙이지 않은 원형부정사(recognize)를 씁니다.

questions.passage: This little device sends a beam of infrared light to gather 3D information about what may lie around the user, including walls and furniture.  The bounced beam conveys that information to the device, which then raises little pins to indicate where those obstacles are.  By “reading” the positions and heights of those pins, the user can understand the arrangement of structures and objects lying ahead and navigate around them.  The heart of this device is a 3D depth sensor connected to a small computer.  Seoyoung coded the computer to control the nine motors lined up in three rows of three so that each motor could move a pin up and down.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, Seoyoung의 장치가 사용자 주변에 무엇이 있는지에 관한 3D 정보를 모으기 위해 내보내는 빛이 무엇인지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'This little device sends a beam of infrared light to gather 3D information about what may lie around the user'에서 장치는 3D 정보를 모으기 위해 적외선 빛(infrared light)을 내보낸다고 했다.
det.tip: sends a beam of infrared light(적외선 빛줄기를 내보낸다)가 근거입니다.

questions.passage: The hardest part was figuring out how to make the app recognize hand gestures.  At times, he felt he was stuck.  When that happened, he would go to sleep.  For Nand, sleeping on it paid off.  He decided to focus on the body parts which are important in signing, such as individual fingertips.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, Nand가 수화에서 중요한 신체 부위 중에서도 특히 집중하기로 한 예가 무엇인지 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'He decided to focus on the body parts which are important in signing, such as individual fingertips.'에서 Nand는 개별 손가락 끝(individual fingertips)에 집중하기로 했다고 했다.
det.tip: such as individual fingertips(개별 손가락 끝과 같은)가 근거입니다.

questions.passage: The bounced beam conveys that information to the device, which then raises little pins to indicate where those obstacles are. By “reading” the positions and heights of those pins, the user can understand the __________ (arrange) of structures and objects lying ahead and navigate around them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 구문 분석: 정관사 the와 전치사 of 사이의 명사 자리이므로 동사 arrange를 명사 arrangement로 바꿔야 한다. '~의 배열'이라는 의미를 나타낸다.
det.tip: the ___ of 구조에서는 동사(arrange)가 아니라 명사(arrangement)가 옵니다.

questions.passage: At least one billion people, or 15% of the world’s population, experience some form of disability.  In order to fully function in everyday life, they need to have the same physical and social access to the places, goods, and services in their communities as everyone else.  For many of them, however, access still remains an issue.  Here are two teenagers who presented new inventions to tackle the issue at an international science competition.  3D Braille Map While thinking about her homework, Seoyoung Jun closed one eye and successfully picked up her pencil holder.  At that moment, she realized that orienting herself in a 3D space didn’t require both eyes.  This surprised her.  With research, she learned that the brain can process 3D information without any vision at all.  And with that, the idea for a new device for people with visual disabilities was born.  Those who have lost sight get their spatial information mainly from touch, not vision.  She based her new navigation device on this fact.  This little device sends a beam of infrared light to gather 3D information about what may lie around the user, including walls and furniture.  The bounced beam conveys that information to the device, which then raises little pins to indicate where those obstacles are.  By “reading” the positions and heights of those pins, the user can understand the arrangement of structures and objects lying ahead and navigate around them.  The heart of this device is a 3D depth sensor connected to a small computer.  Seoyoung coded the computer to control the nine motors lined up in three rows of three so that each motor could move a pin up and down.  The sensor can scan eighteen blocks of space before it, each 0. 06㎥ in size.  When it detects an obstacle in any of these blocks, the corresponding pin rises to either the middle or high position, depending on the height of the obstacle.  By running your hand over the nine pins, you can tell where the obstacles are and how high they are.  When Seoyoung’s device worked for the first time, she didn’t believe it.  To be sure it wasn’t a mistake, she shut it off and rebooted it.  When it worked again, she started screaming with joy.  It had been seven long months of research, building, and testing.  She imagines a future version that could be connected to a smartphone, with more pins and more height positions.  Sign Language-to-Speech App As a coder, Nand Vinchhi wanted to invent something that didn’t require a mechanical device.  One day, he was brainstorming with friends, and the group came up with an idea for an app that could translate sign language.  In the end, they decided not to develop it, but Nand couldn’t stop thinking about the translator.  In just a few months, he developed an app based on artificial intelligence for translating American Sign Language (ASL) in real time.  Nand’s app was basically a speech-to-text app for sign language, where hand movements corresponded to speech.  The hardest part was figuring out how to make the app recognize hand gestures.  At times, he felt he was stuck.  When that happened, he would go to sleep.  For Nand, sleeping on it paid off.  He decided to focus on the body parts which are important in signing, such as individual fingertips.  Using a machine-learning program, he then taught the app to identify those key points in the videos he took.  When the user runs the app, gestures are captured by the camera.  Then, the app uses an algorithm to match the movements with words in ASL, which are turned into text and then spoken aloud.  According to Nand, his system now translates signs with 90. 4% accuracy, and the delay from signing to translation is only about three-tenths of a second.  He imagines the technology could someday become part of existing communication platforms.  That could help ASL speakers communicate with those who don’t know the language.  What these inventions have in common is a creative use of technology to enhance the daily lives of people with disabilities.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 장애가 있는 사람들의 접근성을 높이려 두 십 대가 개발한 창의적 기술(3D 점자 지도, 수화-음성 앱) — 글 전체를 아우르는 중심 소재 ←정답
❌ ② 자율주행차의 경제적 변화는 Read More의 부수적 내용이라 주제가 아님
❌ ③ 대회 우승을 위한 준비 전략은 본문에서 다루지 않음
❌ ④ 시각 장애 예방을 위한 의학 연구는 본문 내용과 무관함
det.tip: 주제는 세부 예시가 아니라 두 발명을 관통하는 중심 내용을 골라야 합니다.

ch: 장애가 있는 사람들의 접근성을 높이기 위해 십 대들이 개발한 창의적인 기술
인공지능 기술이 자율주행차 산업에 가져온 경제적 변화
국제 과학 경진 대회에서 우승하기 위한 효과적인 준비 전략
시각 장애를 예방하기 위한 최신 의학 연구의 성과

questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 대기업의 투자로만 기술이 탄생한다는 것은 본문의 주장과 무관함
❌ ② 장애가 극복할 수 없는 한계라는 것은 발명의 취지와 반대라 부적절
✅ ③ 두 십 대의 창의적 기술 활용이 장애가 있는 사람들의 삶을 개선하고 모두를 위한 더 접근 가능한 세상에 기여한다 — 'a creative use of technology to enhance the daily lives'와 'a more accessible world for all'이 뒷받침하는 핵심 메시지 ←정답
❌ ④ 대회 수상 여부가 성공을 결정한다는 내용은 본문에 없음
det.tip: 요지는 마지막 문단의 '기술로 장애인의 삶을 개선한다'는 핵심 주장에 주목합니다.

ch: 새로운 기술은 반드시 대기업의 막대한 투자를 통해서만 탄생한다.
장애는 일상생활에서 극복할 수 없는 한계로 작용한다.
십 대들의 창의적인 기술 활용이 장애가 있는 사람들의 삶을 개선하고 더 접근 가능한 세상을 만드는 데 기여한다.
과학 경진 대회의 수상 여부가 발명의 성공을 결정한다.

questions.passage: By running your hand over the nine pins, you can tell where the obstacles are and how high they are.  When Seoyoung’s device worked for the first time, she didn’t believe it.  To be sure it wasn’t a mistake, she shut it off and rebooted it.  __________.  It had been seven long months of research, building, and testing.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'그것이 다시 작동했을 때, 그녀는 기뻐서 소리 지르기 시작했다.'

[조건]
(1) again, it, joy, screaming, she, started, When, with, worked를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- When it worked again(시간 부사절): 그것이 다시 작동했을 때
- she(주어) + started(동사): 그녀는 시작했다
- screaming(동명사 목적어): 소리 지르는 것을
- with joy(전치사구): 기뻐서
- 「start + 동명사(-ing)」로 '~하기 시작하다'를 나타낸 문장이며, 시간을 나타내는 When절이 문두에 온다.
det.tip: start는 뒤에 동명사(started screaming)를 취해 '~하기 시작하다'가 됩니다. 시간 부사절 When it worked again이 문두에 옵니다.

questions.wa: When it worked again she started screaming with joy

When it worked again, she started screaming with joy
